narrative:
The 2025 Kansas City Royals were a team that teased promise while constantly undercutting themselves, finishing at 82-80 — a winning record, but not enough to earn a postseason berth. From the opening weeks, the bullpen proved to be the season's defining flaw, with Carlos Estévez and John Schreiber repeatedly surrendering critical leads at the worst possible moments. The offense showed flashes of life, but the Royals too often found themselves clawing back from deficits that should never have existed.

April and early May established an uneasy pattern. The rotation kept Kansas City competitive, but the bullpen was a revolving door of disaster. A brutal April 22nd collapse, where Estévez surrendered a pair of runs on a Jacob Stallings double, set the tone for a troubling trend. The offense occasionally answered — Maikel Garcia's sharp double that same night offered a flicker of resilience — but the Royals couldn't sustain momentum through the early going.

The summer months brought both heartbreak and heroism in equal measure. Jonathan India's three-run blast on July 26th was the kind of moment that made Royal fans believe, and Adam Frazier's clutch double on July 18th was a rallying cry — before Estévez immediately followed with a walk-off home run surrendered to Kyle Stowers, a gut-punch that encapsulated the Royals' maddening duality. Vinnie Pasquantino quietly developed into a power threat, and Nick Loftin delivered timely contributions, but for every spark, a costly bullpen implosion waited around the corner.

As September arrived, the playoff dream slipped away one blown save at a time. Schreiber surrendered a three-run bomb to Jo Adell on September 3rd and was victimized again on September 11th. Adam Frazier provided one last feel-good moment on September 17th with a two-run homer, but a late-season double allowed against Luinder Avila on September 26th served as a fitting coda to a season of near-misses. Kansas City finished two games above .500 — a respectable record that masked a roster capable of more, haunted by a bullpen that too often turned winnable games into lessons in heartbreak.

chapters.title: Early Cracks Appear
chapters.description: April's opening stumbles reveal the bullpen vulnerabilities that will define Kansas City's season.

chapters.title: May Turbulence
chapters.description: The Royals fight to stay afloat as opposing bats punish Kansas City's relief corps while the offense provides only scattered answers.

chapters.title: Midsummer Chaos
chapters.description: A volatile stretch of clutch hits and devastating blown saves leaves Kansas City spinning in place as the trade deadline approaches.

chapters.title: Bursts of Belief
chapters.description: India's three-run homer and Pasquantino's power surge give Royal fans genuine hope for a late-season playoff push.

chapters.title: September Fade
chapters.description: With the playoffs within reach, a beleaguered bullpen and critical late-game failures extinguish Kansas City's postseason hopes for good.
